A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DyaDiT and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Content can be matched across relocation and renumbering, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark and ablation results in Table 1, a 16-participant preference study, and supplementary clustering analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds component comparisons, beat-consistency scores, and statistical significance claims.

M1.justification: The proposed DiT backbone, ORCA, motion dictionary, tokenizer, loss, and conditioning remain. Sections 3.3–3.4 newly describe the projection's MLP implementation and dictionary training without orthogonalization; these disclosures do not establish that the underlying procedure changed. The added model variants are experimental controls.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Seamless Interaction naturalistic subset for upper-body dyadic gesture generation. The supplementary training/test archive selection and social-conditioning coverage are unchanged. Newly disclosed participant demographics do not establish a different study population.

E2.justification: ConvoFusion and Audio2PhotoReal remain the external baselines. However, Table 1 expands its evaluated within-method comparator set with CrossAttn, MD contin, and w/o self. Newly cited interactive-motion methods are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 adds beat consistency (BC) as an evaluation metric, reported for DyaDiT and its variants. The added ablations introduce targeted component controls. Existing dataset splits, FD/diversity definitions, and baseline inference settings of 50 DDIM steps, CFG 2, and 300 frames remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 adds focused tests of ORCA versus standard cross-attention, discrete versus continuous motion representation, and removal of partner-motion conditioning. Existing ablations, interruption examples, and supplementary t-SNE analyses remain, making this a targeted extension of component validation.

E5.justification: v1 provides preference percentages without significance tests. v2 adds chi-square claims with p < 10^-8 against the baseline and p = 1.5 × 10^-4 for personality preference over ground truth. The latter conflicts with the retained statement that this comparison was not conducted. No increased training-run or seed count is reported.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 FD/diversity values and Figure 7 preference percentages are unchanged. v2 adds three ablation rows, BC scores, and significance outcomes. For example, newly reported BC is 0.771 for full DyaDiT and 0.710 for CrossAttn; these are additional comparisons, not improvements over v1's same-setting results.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 adds Equation 3, explicitly specifying a two-layer MLP for the previously abstract projection implementation. This is a limited mathematical specification; the existing loss, projection-subtraction, gating, and dictionary equations otherwise remain equivalent. No proof establishing orthogonality is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: socially conditioned dyadic gesture generation, ORCA-based audio disentanglement, and superior quantitative and perceptual performance. Additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new continuous-dictionary comparison as supporting discrete motion bases and adds a rationale against dictionary orthogonalization. It omits v1's explicit caveat that preferred exaggerated gestures may be less common in real interactions. Future work shifts toward collecting full-body data, while audio-conditioning conflicts remain acknowledged.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the ORCA MLP, joint dictionary training, shared baseline seed-pose conditioning, and participants' ages, CS backgrounds, and session duration. The abstract replaces a release promise with a code/model access link, although the supplement retains the old promise. Detailed supplementary architecture and preprocessing instructions are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 broadens discussion to couple dance and interactive motion, adding Remos, Duolando, and Synergy and Synchrony in Couple Dances. Future work adds BodyContact4D and Contact4D citations. Three speech-separation references are removed as the introduction's framing changes; the central research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The introduction's motivation and several baseline, results, ablation, user-study, and limitations paragraphs are rewritten or condensed. An acknowledgment section is added and supplementary sections are renumbered. The overall narrative structure and substantive supplementary text remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a BC column and three rows, with smaller text and revised highlighting. Figure 2 receives small diagram edits, Figure 3 moves from PDF page 4 to page 5, and page footers disappear. The existing qualitative, preference, and supplementary figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The additional component controls and implementation disclosures improve empirical support and transparency. However, v2 introduces a significant personality-versus-ground-truth claim in Section 5 while explicitly stating that this comparison was not conducted; Figure 7 also lacks it. The PDFs cannot reconcile that statistical claim with the reported study. These benefits and the new reporting inconsistency prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
